method: Original in-order sweep, tree slot retirement with red-black unlink and rotations, selector0 endpoint-ring removal, endpoint clear and pointer-vector reserve run natively; only the allocator vtable entries are supplied. Python composes the sweep with pose_body_tree._Tree.remove(key_size=8), detach_pose_endpoint_rings and reserve_pose_pointer_vector.
comparisons: ordered allocator calls with every argument
all fixture bytes: provider descriptor and slot table, every node byte including retired slots, bodies, records (in and out of the tree), owners, old and new queue arrays
divide-fault occurrence and partial state for divisor 0
coverage: valid red-black trees with 0..39 live nodes and 0..5 free slots
records sharing selector0 rings with out-of-tree records
queue vectors null/nonnull, capacities 0..8, full and nonfull
failure_proof: Starting the sweep at the root instead of the leftmost node fails at case 1.
Advancing the round-robin slot before choosing the owner fails at case 5.
Computing the successor after removal (for nodes with fewer than two children) makes the Python sweep follow retired-slot links and not finish within 60 s; it never passes.
untested_orderings: The owner read between ring removal and endpoint clear is not distinguishable here: neither callee touches the provider.
limits: Ring fixtures are built by the reconstructed attach, not native attach.
Consumers of the owner+0x48 vectors (1989e60 rebalance and any worker-side reuse) are not reconstructed.
No live validation or concurrency guarantee.
